definition: A patch lies closer to end A when both its true-color and false-color halves are predominantly near-black, with faint contrast and few discernible surface features. End B has brighter, varied colors and recognizable landscape structure.
cues: Near-black coverage across both halves is much greater toward A.
Fields, roads, buildings, and vegetation boundaries are readily discernible toward B.
False-color vegetation appears strongly red toward B but is barely visible toward A.
Local color and brightness variation are much weaker toward A.
